uc_external_location_dbutils_fs_ls.interpretation: Unity Catalog External Location with access_point field successfully lists FSx for ONTAP S3 AP contents. The session policy now includes the S3 AP ARN, allowing UC-governed access.

boto3_instance_profile.error: AccessDenied: Could not access through this access point
boto3_instance_profile.interpretation: Instance Profile IAM policy (databricks-fsxn-access-profile) does not have the correct S3 AP permissions. This is an IAM policy issue, not a platform boundary. The UC path works because the Storage Credential role has broader permissions.

superseded_by.source: measured here 2026-08-12, with a native-S3 control in the same session
finding: Registration of an S3 access point path as an External Location succeeds.

The read is what fails: the down-scoped session policy Unity Catalog issues is written with a bucket-form ARN (arn:aws:s3:::<alias>), while AWS authorises an access point request against the access point ARN. The two do not match, and a session policy intersects with the role policy.
The access_point field is not in current Unity Catalog documentation. Whether it was ever released, and why it was removed, is open.
superseded_by.effect_on_this_record: The measurements below (286 objects listed) are what was observed on 2026-05-24 and are unchanged. The conclusion drawn from them was wrong and is retained only as history. Do not cite this record as evidence that Unity Catalog reads FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Points.

conclusion_as_recorded_2026_05_24.key_finding: Setting the access_point field on the External Location resolves the session policy issue. Unity Catalog can now govern access to FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Points.
